key_insight: Neural Fourier Surrogates (NFS) provide a classical baseline that matches the finite Fourier support of data-reuploading QNNs, making QNN comparisons more principled.
engineering_relevance: NFS offers practitioners a practical way to benchmark quantum models against a functionally aligned classical surrogate before claiming quantum advantage.
method: Stochastic classical neural network learns Fourier coefficients over the same finite support as data-reuploading QNNs.
Inspired by Neural Quantum States and Random Fourier Features to mimic QNN-relevant spectral structure.
Evaluated as a classifier against tabular benchmarks and compared to QNNs and classical baselines.
evidence_signal: On tabular benchmark datasets, NFS was broadly competitive with established classical baselines, comparable Random Fourier Features models, and data-reuploading QNNs; spectral analysis on synthetic data further supported the match.
watch_item: Because NFS is a surrogate baseline rather than a proof of equivalence, results may depend on dataset choice, Fourier support assumptions, and implementation details of the QNN architecture.
paper_title: Neural Fourier Surrogates for Data Reuploading Quantum Neural Networks
